claim: At e in [0, 0.8] (N=64, 4L, d64, 600 steps), the headroom-normalised layer-4 accel_step margin, (R2 - control)/(1 - control), at step 600 is 0.475 for seed 70 (R2 0.670 vs best-of-5 control 0.372), 0.455 for seed 71 (0.671 vs 0.396) and 0.475 for seed 72 (0.672 vs 0.375). All three seeds fall inside the predicted [0.44, 0.53] band, and their controls and raw R2 values fall inside the predicted ranges. That puts e<=0.8 between the cited e<=0.7 value (~0.55-0.58) and the e<=0.85 value (~0.38-0.41). Force is much weaker by the same measure: raw margin 0.124-0.150 at layers 1-2 (R2 0.31-0.42 vs control 0.19-0.27), normalised 0.15-0.21, persistent formation late at steps 250-400 and still rising at step 600. accel_step formed at steps 50-100 and levels off at a raw margin of 0.275-0.298.
confidence_note: All 3 seeds completed (none stopped) and land in the predicted band with little spread (0.455-0.475), and the controls are tight (spread 0.011-0.022, so required_margin is 0.1). Four things limit the claim that the decline is gradual. (1) The e<=0.7 and e<=0.85 reference values come from other experiments, and the e<=0.85 value rests on only 2 seeds. (2) With only three ceiling values (0.7, 0.8, 0.85), 'gradual' cannot be told apart from a decline that steepens: the normalised drop is ~0.09 over 0.7->0.8 but ~0.07 over 0.8->0.85, and raw R2 falls ~0.13 over 0.7->0.8 but ~0.11 over 0.8->0.85, which per unit of e looks like steepening. (3) The [0.44, 0.53] band is wide enough to hold several curve shapes. (4) Every arm shares data_seed 0. An e<=0.75 arm far from the interpolated value would change the picture. So would a different data_seed moving the e<=0.8 normalised margin out of the band, for example to >=0.54 or <=0.43. Either could show a step rather than a smooth decline.

notes.text: Response to review r-20261013-004549-e5e2 (issue 0): Accepted. Seed 72's force margin is >= 0.1 at every checkpoint from step 100 onward (0.1032, 0.1103, ... 0.1503), so it forms persistently at step 100. The correct range is 100-400 (seeds 72/70/71: 100/350/400), and 'late' holds only for seeds 70 and 71. In seed 72, force forms 50 steps after accel_step (step 50). The finding's verdict concerns the headroom-normalised accel_step margin at e<=0.8, which is unaffected, so the status stays replicated. This matches seed 72 at e<=0.85, where force also formed early (step 100; f-20261012-231608-1978 note). Seed 72's early force formation looks like a stable property of that seed and not noise.

Response to review r-20261013-004549-e5e2 (issue 0): Accepted. Seed 72's force margin is at or above 0.1 at every checkpoint from step 100 (0.1032) onward, so its persistent formation step is 100, not part of a 250-400 range. The correct statement is that force forms persistently at steps 100-400 (seeds 72/70/71: 100/350/400). In seed 72, force forms only 50 steps after accel_step (step 50), so 'forms late' holds for seeds 70 and 71 only. The accel_step result (normalised margin 0.455-0.475 in all 3 seeds, inside [0.44, 0.53]) is unaffected, and so is the replicated status. The force-timing claim at e<=0.8 should be read as seed-dependent.
